prompt:
A curve shows the variation with time t of the energy E transferred by an electric motor.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Energy against time graph. Vertical axis: energy E in J, scale 0 to 300 J. Horizontal axis: time t in s, scale 0 to 10 s. A smooth curve rises from the origin (0, 0) with increasing gradient. At t = 6.0 s, a tangent to the curve is drawn. The tangent passes through coordinates (2.0 s, 50 J) and (8.0 s, 290 J).]
What is the instantaneous power developed by the motor at t = 6.0 s?

answer.explanation: Instantaneous power is the gradient of the tangent to the energy-time curve at that instant: gradient = Delta E / Delta t = (290 - 50) / (8.0 - 2.0) = 240 / 6.0 = 40 W.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 calculates 240 / 10 = 24 W using the full time scale.
Option 2 estimates power by taking the curve value at 6 s divided by 6 s, confusing average power with instantaneous power.
Option 3 is correct: gradient of tangent = (290 - 50) / (8.0 - 2.0) = 240 / 6.0 = 40 W.
hints: Instantaneous power is the gradient of the tangent drawn at that point.
Find the gradient using the two marked points on the tangent line.
solution: Gradient = (290 J - 50 J) / (8.0 s - 2.0 s) = 240 J / 6.0 s = 40 W. Option C is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Recall that instantaneous power P = dE / dt = gradient of the tangent on an E-t graph.
Identify the two points on the tangent: (2.0, 50) and (8.0, 290).
Calculate gradient: Delta E / Delta t = 240 / 6.0 = 40 W.
